what: Studies of the seven edges on the train pool: filled trades that are not flagged, net R after costs. The exam pool is never read. Research proposes; the mentor decides.

preregistration.statement: Families, buckets, split, minimum sample, correction and pass rule were fixed in the code before any condition result was computed. Nothing was tuned after a run.

families.title: Stop size, reward to risk and side

buckets.rule: One bucket a listed value of a categorical key, one for a yes / no key, two for a numeric key (the lowest and the highest third, cut on the discovery part only). Rows where the key is unknown are left out.

split.by: the first 70 % of an edge's trades in signal-time order, by count; confirmation is the rest
split.baseline: baselines use the period cut of eval.json: 70 % of the way from the first order to the last, by time

passRule: An edge runs condition studies only if its confirmation part holds at least 40 trades; a smaller edge gets one entry saying so and no test.

A condition is tested only when the bucket and the rest each hold at least 20 trades in the discovery part and in the confirmation part. Otherwise: inconclusive, too few trades, and it is not counted as a test.
The measure is net R a trade inside the bucket minus outside it, with a two-sided Welch t, in each part.
Discovery passes at |t| >= 2. A condition that does not pass discovery is inconclusive.

A condition that passes discovery is: rejected when the confirmation difference has the opposite sign; in-sample when the sign holds but the confirmation |t| is under 2; out-of-sample when the sign holds and the confirmation |t| is at least 2.
validated = out-of-sample AND the discovery p-value survives Benjamini-Hochberg at 10 % across every discovery test of the run.
Baseline, regime, book and policy studies are descriptions of the train pool. They carry the label in-sample and are never called an edge.
lessonRule: A draft lesson is written only for a condition that reached out-of-sample or validated.
Bucket worse than the rest: the draft says WAIT when the condition holds. Bucket better than the rest: the draft says TAKE.

Every draft is inactive, carries its evidence (n, net R a trade and t in both parts) and its study id, and says so when the bucket still made money (a WAIT then gives up profit) or still lost money (better than the rest is not good).

pool.note: exam = setups of the exam pool, counted and never read; flaggedTrain = clock-shifted weeks and setups before 2020; unfilled = orders that never filled.

expectedByChance.note: With no real effect anywhere, about 5.8 of the 121 tests would pass discovery (|t| >= 2) and about 0.15 would also confirm with the same sign. The tests overlap, so these are rough.

summary: 121 of 420 pre-registered conditions had enough trades to test. 7 passed discovery; chance alone gives about 5.8.
0 validated, 1 out-of-sample, 4 in-sample only, 2 rejected, 413 inconclusive.
Nothing is validated. No condition here may be called an edge.
proposedLessonsNote: 1 draft lesson, all inactive. Each is one sample on train data: test it on the exam pool before switching it on.

studies.title: The book of seven: overlap, correlation and drawdown
studies.hypothesis: The seven edges do not all win and lose on the same days, so the book falls less than its parts added together.
studies.dataset: Train pool, not flagged, filled trades of all seven edges: 1421, 2020-01-08 to 2026-10-22. 981 days with a closed trade.
studies.method: Each trade is one unit of risk. Net R is booked on the UTC day of the exit. A pair's correlation uses only the days on which both edges closed a trade and needs 20 of them. A trade is active from its signal day to its exit day.
studies.results: More than one edge had a trade active on 48.7 % of 1701 active days, and more than one closed a trade on 24.1 % of 981 closing days. 6 of 21 pairs have enough common days; the largest correlation is geg with gmp, r +0.25 on 23 days (t 1.19). Worst drawdown of the book 36.01 R on daily closes against 101.06 R for the seven edges' own worst drawdowns added together.
studies.limitations: Train pool only: each edge misses its exam months (about 30 %) and the clock-shifted weeks. HistData candles. One sample per edge. Descriptive, not a tested edge. Each edge misses different months, so this is not the live book and its drawdown is understated. Correlations on common days only rest on few days.

studies.title: The decision policy against taking every setup
studies.hypothesis: The trades the policy takes earn more net R a trade than the trades it waits on.
studies.dataset: eval.json 6c59608207b3 (policy policy-1.0, no lessons, no model): 1421 train trades of the seven edges. Feature rows from the matrix for the same trades.
studies.method: TAKE against WAIT is read from eval.json (Welch t). eval.json stores how often each wait reason fired, not what those trades made, so the reason table shows every train trade that carries the feature behind the reason, waited on or not: a proxy.
studies.results: The policy took 486 trades at +0.342 R and waited on 935 at +0.201 R: difference +0.141 R, t 1.17, no measurable difference. The waits skipped +187.95 R in total, most on replica (+97.78 R, n 150). By the feature behind each reason, the most profit sits behind oppLiq (n 1407, total +343.27 R, but that is nearly every trade, so it says little) and htfBias (n 316, total +113.96 R), and the least profit behind momentum (n 303, total +1.55 R). No reason marks a group of trades that lost money.

table.note: reasons: policyWaits = how often the policy named the reason (eval.json: orders for a gate, the strongest contradicting factor otherwise); trades, share, avg, total, t = all train trades carrying the feature (a proxy, not the policy's own waits). The event gate is exact: it fires on every setup with eventNear. The volatility and conflict gates are looser than the feature (the threshold and the conflict rule differ by edge). The unfamiliar-regime gate has no single feature and is not listed.

studies.limitations: Train pool only: each edge misses its exam months (about 30 %) and the clock-shifted weeks. HistData candles. One sample per edge. Descriptive, not a tested edge. The reason table is a proxy: exact net R by wait reason needs the policy walk to store it.
